Package de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.service.resource.control

Class ResourceControlService

java.lang.Object
de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.service.resource.control.ResourceControlService
@Service public class ResourceControlService extends Object
Central entry point for controlling resources. Selects the appropriate transport per command and enforces the permission check (convention: authorization in the service layer via exception).

Slot derivation: The addressed slot is NOT supplied by the client, but determined from the user's active reservation on the resource. A command is therefore only possible while the user holds an ongoing reservation; the slot is always the reserved one. If the user (in the rare case) holds multiple active reservations on the same resource, the slot is ambiguous → SlotNotReservedException (409).

Resolution strategy (capability set with fallback):

  1. Resource has MQTT capability and is online → MQTT
  2. Resource has MQTT capability but is offline → REST fallback, provided a REST endpoint (ip) exists
  3. No MQTT capability → REST
  4. No reachable transport → ResourceOfflineException

REST is the always-active base; MQTT is an optional, additional capability. The MQTT adapter is only present when prioritize.mqtt.enabled=true — therefore it is resolved optionally via an ObjectProvider.

peter haller

  • Method Details

    • sendCommand

      public void sendCommand(Resource resource, String command, String param, PUser user)
      Sends a control command to a resource. Controlling counts as a state change and therefore requires Action.UPDATE permission on the resource. The addressed slot is derived from the user's active reservation.
      Parameters:
      resource - target resource
      command - command identifier
      param - optional free parameter (may be null)
      user - the executing user (permission check + slot derivation)
      Throws:
      org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException - if the user is not allowed to control
      SlotNotReservedException - if the user does not hold a unique active reservation
      ResourceOfflineException - if no reachable transport exists

    • sendCommand

      public void sendCommand(Resource resource, String command, String param, int slot, PUser actor)
      Trusted control path for the platform itself — a BPMN process acting under the system principal (see PlatformGateway), not a user working under a reservation.

      The difference to sendCommand(Resource, String, String, PUser) is where the slot comes from: a process holds no reservation, so it supplies the slot explicitly instead of having it derived. To keep the reservation promise intact, the command is refused (SlotOccupiedException, 409) when that slot currently holds an active reservation held by anyone — a process may only ever command a free slot, never seize a human's reserved window. The permission is still checked against the acting principal: controlling counts as a state change and requires Action.UPDATE, so what a process may control stays a checked property of the system principal rather than an unbounded bypass.

      Parameters:
      resource - target resource
      command - command identifier
      param - optional free parameter (may be null)
      slot - the slot to address, supplied by the process
      actor - the acting principal (permission check)
      Throws:
      org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException - if the principal is not allowed to control the resource
      SlotOccupiedException - if the slot currently holds an active reservation
      ResourceOfflineException - if no reachable transport exists
